purpose: Independent practice and summative evidence of B1.6 (fair sharing with leftovers), B1.7 (1/2 = 2/4 equivalence), B1.8 (unit fraction comparison).
student_learning_goal: I can share a small collection fairly between 2 or 4 friends, draw the share, and tell that one half equals two fourths.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can share a small collection fairly between 2 or 4 friends, draw the share, and tell that one half equals two fourths.
header.character_watermark: Otto in the top-right corner, holding a paper pizza. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Share each collection fairly. Draw the share onto each plate. Circle any leftovers.
parts.visual_layout: Top half of the page. Two share scenes stacked. Scene A: 12 buttons on the left, 4 plates on the right. Scene B: 13 buttons on the left, 4 plates on the right. Below each scene, a blank line for the count per plate.

image_placeholders.description: Two share scenes stacked in B&W line-art. Each scene ~2.5in tall. Scene A: a tray with 12 round buttons on the left, 4 paper plates with light-grey outlines on the right. Scene B: a tray with 13 buttons on the left, 4 plates on the right. Each plate ~1.5in diameter. A small red-circle indicator below each scene for the leftover.
image_placeholders.placement: Top half of the page; two scenes spanning full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P1_TWO_SHARE_SCENES: keywords (buttons, plates, share, leftover) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 3 buttons on each plate, 0 leftover. Scene B: 3 buttons on each plate, 1 leftover.

parts.part_title: Part 2: One Half Equals Two Fourths
parts.student_instructions: Two pizzas. Colour 1/2 of the first pizza. Colour 2/4 of the second pizza. Then write the equation: 1/2 = ___/___.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Two pizzas side-by-side, each ~3in across. Pizza A is divided into 2 halves; Pizza B is divided into 4 fourths. Below: 'I see that 1/2 = ___/___.'

image_placeholders.description: Two circular pizzas in B&W line-art, side by side, each ~3in diameter. Pizza A has one straight line dividing it into 2 halves. Pizza B has two crossed lines dividing it into 4 fourths. Each pizza has a thin black border. Below the pizzas, an equation line.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P2_TWO_PIZZAS: keywords (pizza, halves, fourths) name what the pizzas show.

parts.answer_key: Half of pizza A is shaded. Two fourths of pizza B are shaded. Equation: 1/2 = 2/4.

parts.student_instructions: Four pizzas show different fractions of the SAME size pizza. Draw a line from the BIGGEST piece to the SMALLEST piece in order.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. Four pizzas in a row, each ~1.8in across. Each pizza is divided differently and one slice is shaded: 1/2 (largest shaded), 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 (smallest shaded). The child connects them in order.

image_placeholders.description: Four pizzas in a horizontal row in B&W line-art, each ~1.8in diameter. Pizza 1: divided into 2 halves, 1/2 shaded. Pizza 2: divided into 3 thirds, 1/3 shaded. Pizza 3: divided into 4 fourths, 1/4 shaded. Pizza 4: divided into 5 fifths, 1/5 shaded. Order on the page: random (so the child has to compare).
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P3_FOUR_FRACTIONS: keywords (pizzas, fractions, biggest, smallest) name what the pizzas show.

parts.answer_key: Order from biggest to smallest piece: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5. The child draws lines connecting them in this order.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw a pizza divided into SIX pieces. Colour 1/6. Then compare it to 1/4 — which is bigger?
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone summative worksheet. Hand out at the end of the unit fraction sort. Watch for: (a) Part 1 leftover scenes where children give the leftover to one plate (breaks fairness); (b) Part 2 children who don't see 1/2 = 2/4 — flag for the half-on-fourths overlay reteach; (c) Part 3 children who order biggest-bottom-first (4 > 3 > 2) — the most common B1.8 trap. Use Parts 1-3 as the summative evidence for B1.6/B1.7/B1.8.
